code.source:
CREATE VIEW [Purchasing].[vVendorWithAddresses] AS
SELECT
    v.[BusinessEntityID]
    ,v.[Name]
    ,at.[Name] AS [AddressType]
    ,a.[AddressLine1]
    ,a.[AddressLine2]
    ,a.[City]
    ,sp.[Name] AS [StateProvinceName]
    ,a.[PostalCode]
    ,cr.[Name] AS [CountryRegionName]
FROM [Purchasing].[Vendor] v
    INNER JOIN [Person].[BusinessEntityAddress] bea
    ON bea.[BusinessEntityID] = v.[BusinessEntityID]
    INNER JOIN [Person].[Address] a
    ON a.[AddressID] = bea.[AddressID]
    INNER JOIN [Person].[StateProvince] sp
    ON sp.[StateProvinceID] = a.[StateProvinceID]
    INNER JOIN [Person].[CountryRegion] cr
    ON cr.[CountryRegionCode] = sp.[CountryRegionCode]
    INNER JOIN [Person].[AddressType] at
    ON at.[AddressTypeID] = bea.[AddressTypeID];

-- PostgreSQL conversion of the view Purchasing.vVendorWithAddresses (AdventureWorks2025).
-- Engine: Kiro (mechanical draft via draft-view: identifiers quoted, table names snake_case; kept as the .draft.sql),
-- corrected by Kiro on 2026-11-18 after step 2 found a difference that step 3's generated data had not produced.
-- No human edit; the owner's step 5 review is still to come.
--
-- The source database's collation is SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, so the join on CountryRegionCode is case-insensitive
-- ('us' joins 'US'), accent-sensitive, and ignores trailing spaces ('US ' joins 'US'); PostgreSQL '=' is none of those.
-- Same fix as Person.vStateProvinceCountryRegion: rtrim under a nondeterministic case-insensitive ICU collation.
-- Checked for the text the harness and the fixed cases use (ASCII codes), not for every collation rule.
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS tsql_compat;
CREATE COLLATION IF NOT EXISTS tsql_compat.ci_as_equal (
    provider = icu, locale = 'und-u-ks-level2', deterministic = false
);
-- Adversarial run 2026-11-19 (cases A02-A04): the ICU collation alone differs from SQL Server's on 'Æ' = 'AE' and
-- 'ß' = 'SS' (SQL Server equal, ICU not) and on the Kelvin sign U+212A and the soft hyphen U+00AD (ICU equates U+212A with
-- 'K' and ignores U+00AD; SQL Server does neither). PostgreSQL 18 ignores the ICU strength when tailoring rules are given, so
-- ci_as_key() trims trailing spaces and maps those characters (the last two to private-use code points) before the
-- comparison. Checked for the characters the cases use, not for every collation rule.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION tsql_compat.ci_as_key(s text)
RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
PARALLEL SAFE
AS $fn$
    SELECT replace(replace(replace(translate(rtrim(s, ' '), U&'\00AD\212A', U&'\E000\E001'), 'ß', 'ss'), 'æ', 'ae'), 'Æ', 'AE')
$fn$;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW purchasing.v_vendor_with_addresses AS
SELECT
    v."BusinessEntityID" AS "BusinessEntityID"
    ,v."Name" AS "Name"
    ,at."Name" AS "AddressType"
    ,a."AddressLine1" AS "AddressLine1"
    ,a."AddressLine2" AS "AddressLine2"
    ,a."City" AS "City"
    ,sp."Name" AS "StateProvinceName"
    ,a."PostalCode" AS "PostalCode"
    ,cr."Name" AS "CountryRegionName"
FROM purchasing.vendor v
    INNER JOIN person.business_entity_address bea
    ON bea."BusinessEntityID" = v."BusinessEntityID"
    INNER JOIN person.address a
    ON a."AddressID" = bea."AddressID"
    INNER JOIN person.state_province sp
    ON sp."StateProvinceID" = a."StateProvinceID"
    INNER JOIN person.country_region cr
    ON tsql_compat.ci_as_key(cr."CountryRegionCode") COLLATE tsql_compat.ci_as_equal = tsql_compat.ci_as_key(sp."CountryRegionCode") COLLATE tsql_compat.ci_as_equal
    INNER JOIN person.address_type at
    ON at."AddressTypeID" = bea."AddressTypeID";

notes: Finding (step 2, 2026-11-18): Kiro's draft of Purchasing.vVendorWithAddresses joined CountryRegionCode with PostgreSQL '=', which is case-sensitive and counts trailing spaces. Under the source collation (SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS) 'us' joins 'US' and 'US ' joins 'US'. Step 3 passed because the generated codes never differed only in case or trailing spaces; the fixed cases 'collation' and 'trailing space' failed on PostgreSQL. Fixed in the conversion as for Person.vStateProvinceCountryRegion (rtrim + a case-insensitive ICU collation in the join); both cases are kept as regression cases.

Finding (adversarial run, 2026-11-19, cases A02-A04): the ICU collation in Purchasing.vVendorWithAddresses's CountryRegionCode join differed from SQL Server's on three agent-written inputs: SQL Server joins 'Æ' to 'AE' and 'ß' to 'SS' (ICU does not), and ICU equates the Kelvin sign U+212A with 'K' and ignores the soft hyphen U+00AD (SQL Server does neither). PostgreSQL 18 drops the ICU strength setting when tailoring rules are given, so the conversion maps those characters in tsql_compat.ci_as_key() before comparing under the same collation. Checked for the characters the cases use, not for every collation rule; the three cases are kept as regression cases.

Verified in an isolated scratch database: the original T-SQL is deployed unchanged; tables contain only the columns the object references, with no foreign key constraints and no pre-existing rows. Every foreign-key column is indexed on both engines (a modelling assumption for the runtime step).
